title: Integration and hardening pass over the Wave 1 delivery path
description:
Objective: gate the epic where the slices could not see each other. Wave 1 touched shared schema, the tool registry, the wire protocol to both clients and both launcher scripts, so the composed result needs a pass no individual task could perform.

Deliverable: one end-to-end pilot run of the whole flow on a throwaway project, a full regression across every package the epic touched, the epic's documentation sweep, and an adversarial read of the entire epic diff looking for producer and consumer contracts that drifted apart, duplicated stores, and error paths that only fail in combination.

The pilot exercises the real path once: claim opens an attempt, the worker completes, the attempt holds finalizing, the wrapper freezes a candidate and runs the gate in a clean workspace, QA approves against that exact candidate, the receipt records the landing, and a dependent task becomes claimable only then. Then repeat it with a forced gate failure and confirm the dependent stays withheld and the bytes went to a rescue ref.

Not in scope: new features. Any defect found that is not a contract drift between Wave 1 slices is filed as a new task rather than fixed here.

Verification: the full suites named in the Definition of Done, all green, with counts recorded.
definitionOfDone: All six acceptance cases in src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts are unskipped and passing with no assertion edited since they were authored

Full regression green with recorded counts: npm test in packages/moe-daemon, packages/moe-proxy and packages/moe-claude-plugin, cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test, cd moe-vscode and npm test plus npm run compile
Both launcher harnesses pass: bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh, run sequentially on a quiet box with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180
The end-to-end pilot runs on a throwaway project for both the success path and a forced gate failure, and its transcript is recorded in the completion summary
docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/MCP_SERVER.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md describe the attempt, candidate, check run, review, receipt and deliveryPolicy surfaces as shipped
An adversarial pass over the whole epic diff is recorded, naming every contract drift, duplicated helper and combined-failure path found, each either fixed here or filed as a new task
taskRails: This is the epic's only concentrated gate; do not add sibling evidence or hardening rows.
Defects outside Wave 1 contract drift are filed as new tasks, not fixed here.
Run the launcher harnesses sequentially; they flake under a busy fleet.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4a — the end-to-end pilot, success path (DoD 4, first half).

Write `scripts/tests/wave1-pilot.mjs`: a MANUAL, opt-in harness (never invoked by postflight.sh or CI) that runs the whole Wave 1 flow once against a throwaway project, with the REAL daemon, the REAL proxy and the REAL launcher — which is what no acceptance case does end to end. It exists so QA can re-run the pilot instead of trusting a transcript.

Shape:
- Build first: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build` and the same in packages/moe-proxy (the pilot runs dist/, and a stale dist would test yesterday's daemon). Note in the step report that a rebuilt dist only reaches the live fleet on its next daemon restart.
- Create a temp project outside the repo, `git init` it with a fixed identity, a tracked gate script and one owned file, and write `.moe/project.json` with deliveryPolicy `local-branch`, a qualityGate, qualityGateScope everyTask, autoCommit true and a consolidationBranch.
- Start the daemon on it (`node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js start --project <tmp>`), wait for `.moe/daemon.json` and GET /health.
- Seed an epic and two tasks: A (WORKING, one step) and B with `dependsOn: [A]`.
- Run `scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}` for a worker seat with a fake CLI that edits the owned file and drives get_context / start_step / complete_step / complete_task through the real proxy.
- Then a QA seat (or moe-call.sh) claims A for REVIEW and calls qa_approve with the candidate id the wrapper recorded.

Assert, and print, each link of the chain: the claim opened attempt generation 1; complete_task left it finalizing and the row unassigned; a QA claim before the finalize is refused ATTEMPT_FINALIZING; the wrapper froze a candidate and ran the gate in a clean workspace (its check run is runner-observed, exit 0, bound to the candidate tree); the landing moved the target once; the receipt names that candidate with target before/after and the landed revision; finalize_attempt closed the attempt; qa_approve refused a superseded candidate id and accepted the current one; B was NOT claimable before A had its evidence and IS after.

Error handling: every external step is bounded by a timeout with the daemon log tail printed on failure, the daemon is stopped and the temp project removed in a finally, and the script exits non-zero on the first broken link rather than continuing. It must never touch the repository's own .moe/ or the live daemon's port — let the daemon pick its port and read it from the temp project's daemon.json.

Record the full transcript for the completion summary.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4b — the pilot's forced gate failure (DoD 4, second half).

Run the same pilot with the gate rigged to fail (a mode flag on the script, for example `--gate-fails`, that writes a gate script exiting non-zero on the delivered tree).

Assert, and print: the wrapper recorded the candidate and a check run with the real non-zero exit code and source runner-observed; the delivery target did NOT move; the bytes are parked on a `refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts>` ref that still contains the edit; the failure is reported as MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE with a PUSH-BLOCKED line; no delivery receipt exists; and B stays unclaimable — with the refusal naming the missing `required-check:<command>` evidence, not just an unmet status.

The last point is the drift this half is really probing: the wrapper sends the gate command it ran and delivery/policy.ts builds `required-check:<trimmed command>` for comparison. If the two spellings ever differ — by whitespace, quoting or platform — dependents are withheld from a PASSING gate and nothing says why. Assert the recorded check command and the policy token match exactly, on both the pass and the fail run.

Same error handling as the success run: bounded, self-cleaning, non-zero on the first broken link. Record the transcript.

implementationPlan.note:
Round 2 doc fixes: all 11 QA items, plus the same claims wherever else they appear in the 4 docs. Each was checked against the code first (step-1 note).

ARCHITECTURE.md, Delivery Path:
- (1, 2) Intro and table: the plan revision covers every task; the attempt covers every claim that assigns a named worker. Candidate, CheckRun and DeliveryReceipt exist for gated completions only, and a Review only when the task has a candidate. There is a new "Exists for" column.
  - The gate runs only on a worker's completion landing in a git repository, when the command is non-blank, autoCommit is on, scope is everyTask or the task is epic-final, and MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE != 1.
  - Step 3 is conditional ("When a gate will run"). Step 5 records a Review only on a task with a candidate: naming another candidate is refused CANDIDATE_MISMATCH, and naming none binds the current one with NO-REVIEWED-CANDIDATE.
  - New no-gate paragraph: none of the four records is written. The record_commit entry in task.commits is the landing evidence; finalize_attempt closes the attempt with the landing's outcome (nothing-to-commit for autoCommit:false or no git).
- (3) Invariant: the daemon never writes git state, lands, pushes or runs a gate. Its one git call is the read-only `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` handoff fingerprint (util/diskState.ts, from claim_next_task and release_task).
- (4) Step 2: only an explicit-taskId claim by another seat is refused; the ranked pool and wait_for_task skip the row.
- (5) Step 6: the pool and wait_for_task skip a WORKING dependsOn dependent; only an explicit claim is refused DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING; a blockedOnTaskIds wait is not auto-unblocked; dependsOn never gates PLANNING or REVIEW.
- (6) Restart: no idle signal releases a WORKING or PLANNING seat. The REVIEW self-heal is the exception (reviewStaleTimeoutMs, 30 min), and it closes the owner's running or reconciling attempt.

SCHEMA.md:
- (7) Intro: record_candidate and release_task refuse ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED. finalize_attempt answers a closed attempt idempotently before the fence, so it refuses only a generation mismatch on the open attempt.
- (8) New phase row: reconciling -> finalizing via complete_task.
- (4) Closing paragraph: explicit-taskId claim versus skip.
- (9) The durable landing record is the task.commits completion entry, plus a DeliveryReceipt when the landing ran a gate.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 7 — the adversarial pass over the whole epic diff (DoD 6). Work the surface from step 1 with this checklist; record EVERY finding with file:line and a verdict of fixed-here or filed, and name the new task id for each filed one (task rail 2).

1. Revision-shape drift, the one that already bit once (task-9e851d4e reopen 1): candidateStore's 7-40 hex SHA_RE, receiptStore's exactly-40, checkRunStore, deliveryProjection, finalizeAttempt's case-insensitive 40, and both wrappers' own checks. Trace one short (7-hex) candidate treeSha end to end and one uppercase revision; anywhere a producer is laxer than its consumer is drift.
2. Two builders for one code name: claimGuards.attemptFinalizingRefusal and claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal both raise ATTEMPT_FINALIZING. Confirm identical context keys and the retryable flag, and that the wire form (McpAdapter forwards only {tool, codeName}) still names the held attempt in the message.
3. Registry and dispatch: every Wave 1 tool is in getTools() exactly once, none of the new ones sets blocking:true by accident, and each holds the mutex the way its store expects.
4. Durable-first order in all six stores: persist before publish, and no partial transition left unrepaired. A store that emits before it writes is drift against the epic's architecture note.
5. Evidence producers versus consumers: the wrapper's recorded check command versus policy.ts's required-check token (step 4 proves it at runtime); the attempt outcomes the wrapper sends (landed / nothing-to-commit / rescued / failed) versus what finalize_attempt accepts; the candidate fields the wrapper freezes versus what qa_approve binds and deliveryProjection serves.
6. Duplicated helpers: SHA validators, id generators, revision comparators, 'is this task's evidence sufficient' logic. One rule, one home — anything copied is either deleted here or filed.
7. Combined-failure paths no single slice could test: a gate failure plus a QA claim; a daemon restart between candidate and check run; a receipt refused while the attempt is finalizing; autoCommit=false and manual/no-git projects across the whole chain (epic rail 5).
8. Client contracts: the JetBrains parser and presentation against deliveryProjection's served fields; VS Code untouched — confirm nothing serves it a field it will choke on.

Only Wave 1 contract drift is fixed here, and a fix lands with a test that fails on the old behaviour (epic rail 4). Everything else is filed with moe.create_task, including anything found in the three in-flight cards' scope. Keep this card inside its file budget: if a fix would touch more than a couple of files, file it instead and say why.

issues.description: Delivery Path intro ('A task reaches DONE through six durable records'), table and steps 3-5 present Candidate/CheckRun/DeliveryReceipt as universal. Both wrappers record them ONLY for a completion that runs settings.qualityGate ('Only a completion that will actually run a gate freezes and records a candidate', moe-agent.ps1:3943-3946, moe-agent.sh:3963-3966). Gate chosen at ps1:3794-3800: non-blank, autoCommit on, scope everyTask or epic-final, MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE unset.

Same section: with no gate (the default; this repo sets none) a task reaches DONE with planRevision + ExecutionAttempt only, and the landing evidence is the task.commits completion entry. A Review is recorded only when the task has a candidate (state/reviewStore.ts:237), then even if QA names none (binds current + NO-REVIEWED-CANDIDATE, :239-245). Fix: mark the gated-only records, make steps 3-5 conditional on a gate running, add a one-line no-gate path.

Invariant 'It never runs git' is false: the daemon runs a read-only `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` for handoff disk-state signatures (util/diskState.ts:43-57; called from claimNextTask.ts and releaseTask.ts:166). State what holds: it never writes git state, lands, pushes or runs the gate; name the read-only fingerprint as the exception.

Step 2 'every other seat's claim of the task ... refused with retryable ATTEMPT_FINALIZING': only an explicit claim_next_task naming the taskId is refused (claimNextTask.ts:403-406). The ranked pool (the wrappers' only path) and wait_for_task SKIP the row silently (claimNextTask.ts:453-458, 'SKIPPED, never refused'). The same wording is in docs/SCHEMA.md's ExecutionAttempt closing paragraph; fix both.

Step 6: a dependent of a DONE prerequisite lacking its required check is skipped by the ranked pool; DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING is thrown only on an explicit taskId claim, and dependsOn gates WORKING claims only (util/claimEligibility.ts:38-39; claimNextTask.ts:417-418, 452). Say that instead of 'keeps its dependents unclaimable'.

Restart sentence 'holds its row until the runner reattaches or reconcileWindowMs passes; no idle signal releases a seat' is false for REVIEW rows: the REVIEW self-heal (state/sweeps.ts:459-492) releases a REVIEW row whose owner is silent past reviewStaleTimeoutMs (default 30 min), which closes the owner's reconciling attempt via closeHandedBackAttempts (state/taskStore.ts:245-248). Name the exception.

ExecutionAttempt intro lists moe.finalize_attempt among the fenced tools that refuse a no-longer-current attempt with ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED. It answers an already-closed attempt with an idempotent success BEFORE the fence (tools/finalizeAttempt.ts:191-202), and a superseded attempt is always closed, so it refuses ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED only for a generation mismatch on the open attempt. record_candidate and release_task do refuse as stated.

Phases table shows only running -> finalizing. complete_task moves whatever open attempt currentAttempt returns (tools/completeTask.ts:149-152), so reconciling -> finalizing also happens (a CLI that survived a daemon restart completes before its runner reattaches). Add that row.

ExecutionAttempt closing paragraph: 'the durable landing record is the DeliveryReceipt' holds only for gated landings (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:269 already says 'Every landed gated candidate'). Any other landing's durable record is the task.commits completion entry written by moe.record_commit. Fix the sentence.

deliveryPolicy row 'so a commit landed from an earlier round never counts' (and MCP_SERVER.md '(a completion commit from an earlier round does not count ...)') overclaims: a set_task_status reopen adds no rejectionHistory entry and keeps workStartedAt (util/reopen.ts:47-56 clears only reviewStartedAt), so the prior round's completion commit still counts (delivery/policy.ts:128-132). Scope it to qa_reject-opened rounds or state the exception.

Same row: 'The wrapper runs the gate only when ...' omits MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1 (moe-agent.ps1:1989, moe-agent.sh:7121). It skips the gate for that run while a strict policy still demands required-check:<qualityGate> (the daemon cannot see the env), so qa_approve is refused DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING. Name it.

rejectionHistory.reason:
DoD 5 fails. The two doc sections this card wrote, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Delivery Path" and docs/SCHEMA.md "## ExecutionAttempt", describe several Wave 1 surfaces differently from the shipped code. The main case: they present Candidate, CheckRun, DeliveryReceipt and Review as the path every task takes. Both wrappers record them only for a completion that actually runs settings.qualityGate. The gate is unset by default and this repo sets none, so a default task reaches DONE with only its ExecutionAttempt and a task.commits entry. Two parentheticals in CONFIGURATION.md and MCP_SERVER.md also overclaim.

Everything else is verified green; see comment-61f95d16. Acceptance 6/6, unchanged since b5925e2 apart from skip toggles. Daemon 2109/2109 with tsc 0; proxy 62; plugin 13; JetBrains 197; VS Code 113 plus compile; parity PASS; postflight.sh 64+28 PASS. The pilot was re-run on pwsh and sh, success and forced-fail, and the padded gate is red on the old policy.ts and green on HEAD end to end.

Round 2 is docs-only: fix the 11 items listed. No code, test or harness re-run is needed; run `npm run lint`. The QA-found code defects are already filed (task-e7cf44d7, task-dad7eda4, SHA-256 note on task-31fe6dc8), so do not re-file them.
